title: Grateful Dead Live at San Francisco Civic Auditorium on 1983-12-28
lineage: MAC > Nakamichi DR-8 (Dolby) > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab > CD-Wave > TLH > FLAC 2496. Taped and transferred by Andrew F. 05/2009 + VID (no shn id) used for patching and timing reference - matrix mixing by Kevin Tobin
source: flac16; Matrix 3 Source Mix - SBD (shnid=96172) Recording Info:SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLII-S90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> r8brain PRO v1.5 -> FLAC/16; All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller + AUD (shn id 99126) FOB AUD: Sennheiser MD-421's > patched thru one deck (Nak 550) > Marantz PMD-340 > Sony UCX-S 90's, with Dolby. ai_review.summary: Matrix mix balances the board tape’s quirks, giving a decent listen though Bob’s guitar still dominates and the show feels solid yet spotty.
ai_review.review: The matrix version of this 1983‑84 show improves on the original board tape by blending audience ambience with the mix, but Bob Weir’s rhythm guitar remains unusually forward, sometimes masking Jerry Garcia’s lead on “Stranger.” Overall the performance is good for the era, though listeners should expect the typical spotty moments of the mid‑80s Dead.

ai_rating.rationale: Only one moderate (3‑star) review; comments praise the matrix mix but note balance issues and spotty performance, leading to an overall average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Matrix blend offers a clearer picture than pure board tape; Bob's guitar is still overly forward and Jerry's lead on “Stranger” is buried, but the mix overall is listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: No specific comments on set pacing; reviewer describes the show as generally good despite typical mid‑80s inconsistencies.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His lead guitar is barely audible on “Stranger” in the original board tape, though the matrix mix brings him up a bit.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob's rhythm guitar is unusually loud, providing energy but sometimes overpowering other parts.
